    {
      "startEvent": 111,
      "endEvent": 112,
      "contextStartEvent": 59,
      "contextEndEvent": 174,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "God is the only thing that can ultimately sustain the weight of your greatest desires and your meaning.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The exclusive conclusion goes beyond the reported church-health associations and criticism of national identity. However, B supplies an argument about finite commitments, suffering, and durable identity at E125–174, explicitly calling part conjecture. Whether this maxim substitutes for establishing exclusivity or summarizes that ordinary argument remains uncertain; objections are not expressly excluded."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 129,
      "endEvent": 145,
      "contextStartEvent": 113,
      "contextEndEvent": 174,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "If you worship something finite, it will eat you alive.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "fear",
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B adopts the attributed maxim and extends it into inevitable secular failure under suffering and increasing Christian meaning. The finite-versus-eternal distinction supplies a rationale, but not why every finite commitment must fail or Christian meaning must grow. Later conjectural identity explanations at E161–174 soften the account without earning these categorical guarantees."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 212,
      "endEvent": 218,
      "contextStartEvent": 198,
      "contextEndEvent": 243,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Don't wave your fist in God's face when you suffer because it's not God's fault.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The repeated unfair-life/fair-God formula expressly redirects suffering-based blame away from God before considering its merits. Yet E205–209 supplies a human-rebellion explanation, so substitution is uncertain rather than established. A later raises God's permission of Job's suffering at E312–329; B subsequently concedes unanswered intellectual questions at E339–352."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 402,
      "endEvent": 408,
      "contextStartEvent": 358,
      "contextEndEvent": 420,
      "speaker": "U",
      "quote": "Who are you to question me in this sense?",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The guest endorses God's right to rebuke Job and invokes creation, potentially treating superior power or knowledge as grounds to reject questioning. However, E392–404 calls creation evidence, and E409–420 stresses evidence preceding correction. This may be a disputed evidential argument rather than unrestricted protection; the quoted challenge is not a settled-conclusion slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 536,
      "endEvent": 542,
      "contextStartEvent": 529,
      "contextEndEvent": 559,
      "speaker": "U",
      "quote": "God has given enough evidence for those who are truly going to believe and are open to it",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame",
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The adopted Pascal maxim sorts evidential adequacy by openness to belief, after surviving doubt is attributed to emotional or volitional bias at E536–538. No independent reason establishes those motives. E543–559 offers a relationship-versus-fear rationale for limited revelation, but does not justify making continued disbelief evidence of the doubter's closedness."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 561,
      "endEvent": 573,
      "contextStartEvent": 560,
      "contextEndEvent": 580,
      "speaker": "U",
      "quote": "Any example we get of doubting in scripture where it's consistent, eventually that's a sin.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Persistent doubt is initially moralized, potentially discouraging sustained objections without assessing them. But E564–573 distinguishes intellectual truth-seeking from divided conduct and expressly allows honest doubt that perhaps leads to belief. That qualification prevents establishing blanket protection. This is an interpretive argument about doubt, not a compact affirmation replacing reasons."
    }
  ],
